2048.blurb: Slide and merge tiles to reach 2048.

chess.name: Chess
chess.blurb: Play the computer or a friend.

2048.a1: Every move slides all tiles as far as they go in one direction. Two tiles with the same number that touch merge into one with their sum. After each move a new 2 or 4 appears. Make a 2048 tile to win.
2048.q2: How do I move on a phone?
2048.a2: Swipe on the board in the direction you want, or use the arrow buttons next to it. On a keyboard use the arrow keys or W A S D.
2048.a3: Yes. When the 2048 tile appears, choose Keep going to aim for 4096 and beyond.
2048.a4: Keep your biggest tile in one corner and build a chain of falling numbers along the edge next to it. Avoid the move that pulls the big tile out of its corner.
2048.a5: Yes, in this browser only, together with your best score. Nothing is sent to cv.cm.

dinosaur-game.q1: How do you play the dinosaur game?
dinosaur-game.a1: Press Space or the Up arrow, or tap the game, to start and to jump over cacti. Press Down to duck under birds or to fall faster. The game speeds up the longer you run.
dinosaur-game.q2: Is this the same as Chrome's offline game?
dinosaur-game.a2: Yes. It is the T-Rex runner from the Chromium source code, released under a BSD licence, so you can play it without turning off your internet.
dinosaur-game.q3: Does it work on a phone?
dinosaur-game.a3: Yes. Tap the game area to jump. Turn the phone sideways for a wider view.
dinosaur-game.q4: Why does the screen turn dark?
dinosaur-game.a4: After 700 points the game switches between day and night now and then, as in Chrome.
dinosaur-game.a5: Yes, your best score is kept in this browser.

mahjong.q1: How do you play mahjong solitaire?
mahjong.a1: Remove the tiles in matching pairs. A tile can be taken only when nothing lies on top of it and its left or right side is free. Clear every tile to win.
mahjong.a2: Identical tiles match. The four seasons match each other, and the four flowers match each other, even though their pictures differ.
mahjong.a3: Yes. Every deal is built so that it can be cleared. If you get stuck, use Undo, Hint or Shuffle.
mahjong.a4: It rearranges the tiles still on the board so that they can again be cleared. Tiles you removed stay removed.
mahjong.q5: Is this the same as Shanghai or tile matching?
mahjong.a5: Yes. Mahjong solitaire is also called Shanghai or mahjong connect. It uses mahjong tiles but not the rules of four-player mahjong.

chess.a1: There are five levels. Beginner makes many mistakes; Master plays at the full strength of the Stockfish engine and beats almost every human player.
chess.q2: How do I move a piece?
chess.a2: Tap a piece, then tap one of the marked squares. Castling, en passant and promotion are supported; when a pawn reaches the last rank you choose the new piece.
chess.a3: Yes. Choose Two players and take turns on one screen.
chess.q4: When is the game a draw?
chess.a4: On stalemate, threefold repetition, the fifty-move rule, or when neither side has enough material to mate.
chess.q5: Does the engine send my moves anywhere?
chess.a5: No. Stockfish runs in your browser. The game is saved in this browser only.

chinese-chess.q1: How do you play Chinese chess?
chinese-chess.a1: Red moves first. The goal is to checkmate the opposing general. Pieces move on the points of a 9 × 10 board; the river divides it and the general and advisors stay in their palace.
chinese-chess.a2: The chariot moves like a rook, the horse one point straight then one diagonally (blocked by a piece next to it), the elephant two points diagonally without crossing the river, and the cannon moves like a chariot but captures by jumping over exactly one piece.
chinese-chess.q3: Can the two generals face each other?
chinese-chess.a3: No. A move that leaves the two generals on the same file with nothing between them is not allowed.
chinese-chess.a4: A side that keeps giving check to repeat the position loses. Other repetitions are a draw.
chinese-chess.a5: There are four levels, from Beginner to Expert. The engine is XiangQi Wizard Light and runs in your browser.

2048.s1b: Use the arrow keys, W A S D, a swipe or the arrow buttons. All tiles move together.
2048.s2b: Two touching tiles with the same number join into their sum and add it to your score.
2048.s3b: Keep the biggest tile in a corner. When no move is left the game ends; tap New game to try again.

dinosaur-game.lead: Play the dinosaur game in three steps.
dinosaur-game.s1b: Press Space or the Up arrow, or tap the game area.
dinosaur-game.s2b: Jump over cacti; press Down to duck under birds.
dinosaur-game.s3b: When you crash, press Space or tap to run again. Your best score is kept.

mahjong.lead: Play mahjong solitaire in three steps.
mahjong.s1b: Choose a layout such as the turtle and tap New game. Every deal can be cleared.
mahjong.s2b: Tap two matching tiles that are free: nothing on top, and the left or right side open.
mahjong.s3b: Use Hint to see a pair, Undo to take a move back, and Shuffle when no pair is left.

chess.s1b: Play the computer at one of five levels as White or Black, or two players on one screen.
chess.s2b: Tap a piece, then a marked square. The last move and a king in check are highlighted.
chess.s3b: Checkmate wins; stalemate and repetition draw. Use Undo to take a move back.

chinese-chess.lead: Play Chinese chess in three steps.
chinese-chess.s1b: Play the computer at one of four levels as Red or Black, or two players on one screen.
chinese-chess.s2b: Tap a piece, then a marked point. Red moves first.
chinese-chess.s3b: Win by leaving the other general no escape. Use Undo to take a move back.
